title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
abstract: arXiv:2611.18104v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. Preregistered experiments trace the contagion to imitation of the history's style. History also moves a model away from its own fingerprint: active probes are not camouflaged, but when calibrated on fresh conversations they flag \emph{honest} models on long contexts at

translated_title: 传染性指纹：当大语言模型继承另一个模型的身份时
translated_abstract: 分类器用来识别文本背后大语言模型的“指纹”通常被视为模型的固定属性。我们证明这种指纹是会传染的：一个接续由另一个模型开始的对话的模型，会继承那个模型的指纹。这破坏了对API中转服务的审计——此类服务可以用客户付费的模型来回应对话的前几轮，然后悄悄将剩余部分转交给更便宜的模型。在这种转手之后，文本分类器对替代模型的检测率从0.97降至0.72（DeepSeek替换Claude Sonnet），在同类厂商降级（Haiku）的情况下从0.87降至0.54，而且在转手数据上重新训练只能修复训练中见过的替代模型。预注册实验将这种传染追溯到对历史对话风格的模仿。对话历史还会使模型偏离其自身的指纹：主动探测不会被伪装，但当基于新鲜对话进行校准时，它们会在长上下文中误报诚实的模型。
tldr: 本文发现大语言模型的指纹具有“传染性”——接续其他模型对话的模型会继承前者的指纹，导致API中转中的模型偷换检测率大幅下降（如从0.97降至0.72），其根源在于模型对历史对话风格的模仿。
en_tdlr: LLM fingerprints are contagious—a model continuing another model's conversation inherits its fingerprint, undermining API relay audits with detection rates dropping sharply (e.g., 0.97 to 0.72), traced to imitation of the conversation history's style.
